hints.title: Two-Way Neighbor Constraint Decoupling
hints.text: Children with higher ratings must get more candy than their immediate neighbors. How can separating left-to-right and right-to-left dependencies satisfy both neighbors?

hints.title: Forward Backward Extreme Envelope Invariant
hints.text: A forward pass guarantees the left-neighbor condition, while a backward pass satisfies the right-neighbor condition by taking maximums.

hints.title: Bidirectional Array Scan Procedure
hints.text: Initialize candy array of length n with 1s. Traverse from left to right, setting candy to previous plus 1 if current rating exceeds left neighbor. Traverse from right to left, setting candy to maximum of current and right plus 1 if rating exceeds right neighbor. Sum all candies.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Propagating neighbor updates repeatedly until equilibrium can degrade to O(N^2) in worst-case mountain profiles.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two linear passes compute the globally minimal candy allocation in O(N) time with O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why the max operator on the second pass preserves both left and right neighbor constraints.
